subject: Planned EU regional node regeneration + kernel tuning — impact and mitigation
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Horizon Analytics <ops@horizon-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Planned EU regional node regeneration + kernel tuning — impact and mitigation

Hi Tomas and team,

We wanted to let you know about a scheduled maintenance window in our EU regions on Thursday, 6 May. This is a targeted node regeneration and kernel/driver tuning pass intended to improve long-tail latency for multi-instance workloads and enable a new network interrupt mitigation we tested in canary. High-level details below: 

- Window: 2027-05-06 03:00 — 07:00 UTC (staged across eu-west-1 then eu-west-2)
- Scope: rolling node regeneration (no full pool drain) + kernel tuning patch 1.2.9 (non-disruptive for most customers)
- Expected customer impact: brief reconnects for in-flight sessions during instance reboot; transient per-request latency spikes up to ~20s for shortest windows when KV caches rehydrate. We expect <1% request retries for customers on shared pools; customers on Dedicated capacity could see longer reconnect windows if pinned single-instance machines are affected.

Mitigations we are applying:
- Staged rollout with traffic shift to nearby EU region during each node reboot
- KV cache warmup preserved for pinned sessions where possible; we will pre-warm for customers who opt in
- Canary verification and automatic rollback if error rates exceed our SLO thresholds

Action items for you:
- If you run on Dedicated pools and would like pre-warm or a manual maintenance pin, reply with your pool ID(s) and we’ll coordinate a no-impact slot.
- If you have any high-priority jobs during that window, tell us and we’ll exclude relevant instances where feasible.

Attached is a short impact matrix and the maintenance plan (eu-node-regen-plan-v2.pdf). I’ll follow up after execution with a short post-execution note.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Reliability Manager — Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the heads up. A couple quick questions: 

1) We run mixed traffic (shared + some dedicated burst capacity). Our dedicated pool IDs: dp-HA-3, dp-HA-7. Can you confirm if pinned instances in a dedicated pool will be rotated during this window? If so, what is the expected reconnection flow?

2) You mentioned pre-warm "for customers who opt in" — what does that entail operationally and is there any cost/latency tradeoff?

3) Is there any action we need to take in our retry/backoff logic, or will the SDK handle the reconnections automatically?

If helpful we can provide a short list of critical flows to exclude.

—Tomas

ops@horizon-analytics.com

Marissa / Ben — quick internal note and request: 

- Tomas asked whether Dedicated pools dp-HA-3 and dp-HA-7 will be rotated. Per the runbook: Dedicated pools are eligible for per-instance regen if underlying hardware requires the kernel tuning; we should only touch a single instance at a time and maintain the pinned routing where possible.
- Please prepare a pre-warm slot for dp-HA-3 and dp-HA-7 and flag them so we do not reassociate customer traffic with any new instances until the KV warmup succeeds.
- Appsec/telemetry: increase error-rate alert threshold temporarily to avoid noisy page alerts while we observe reconnection behavior; Marissa please coordinate with on-call.

Also, Ben — confirm that the fallback routing to eu-west-3 is enabled and that the autoscaler won't scale down below min capacity during the window.

I'll reply to Tomas once you confirm.

Naomi

Subject: Re: Planned EU regional node regeneration + kernel tuning — impact and mitigation

Hi all — confirmed: 
- We will exclude dp-HA-3 and dp-HA-7 from aggressive rotation unless the kernel patch requires it; we will perform a single-instance regen per pool and ensure traffic stays pinned where possible.
- Pre-warm plan: we will run an automated pre-warm for the two pools 30 minutes before their instance window and hold sticky routing until KV cache hits reach the configured threshold. No extra charge for pre-warm; it’s operational time from our side.
- Fallback routing: eu-west-3 is enabled; autoscaler will keep min capacity, Marissa has set the temporary scale guard.

Naomi — runbook update link: https://redwood-internal.company/runbooks/eu-node-regen-v2 (I updated the step for Dedicated pools).

Ben
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Hi Tomas — quick follow-up before we start. 

- We will run the dedicated pre-warm for dp-HA-3 and dp-HA-7 at 02:30 UTC; those pools will be marked as pre-warmed and excluded from reassociation until cache thresholds are met.
- No action required from your side; the SDK handles transparent reconnects. For safety, please ensure your client retry backoff uses a max-jitter window (we recommend exponential backoff with max 30s).
- If you need an exclusion for a specific flow, reply and we’ll schedule a custom slot.

I’ll post a short execution note when the first tranche completes.

Thanks — Naomi

Subject: Post-execution: EU node regen complete + follow-up notes

Tomas / Horizon team —

Thanks for your patience. We completed the staged regeneration and kernel tuning on eu-west-1 and eu-west-2 overnight. Highlights and quick post-exec notes: 

- Execution: all stages completed as planned; dp-HA-3 and dp-HA-7 were pre-warmed and had no observable traffic loss beyond short TCP-level reconnects (client SDK-level retries handled recoveries).
- Metrics: median P95 tail latency improved by ~12% for multi-instance inference; transient error-rate bumps were <0.6% during per-instance reboots and returned to baseline within 4 minutes of each instance completing warmup.
- Lessons/actions: we will adjust the pre-warm threshold upward for heavy KV workloads to shave another ~5–7% off tail latency. Runbook updated and small postmortem is attached.

Attachments: eu-node-regen-postmortem.pdf (application/pdf)

If you have any anomalies to report or want a deeper run-through of metrics, let me know and we can set a short follow-up call.

Best,
Naomi
